mechanism_narrative: The workplace series has recovered 8.0 points over the four weekly means (from -33.4 at t-3w to -25.4 at t-0w), showing that commuting and daytime population outflows are returning to Milan. Returning commuters mechanically raise weekday footfall in retail corridors, so RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days will be higher than its last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -33.4 at t-3w to -25.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days fails to exceed its last-28-day mean whenever WORKPLACES improves by at least 5 points across the trailing four weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: A single-week transit rebound of 6.8 points (TRANSIT from -50.4 at t-1w to -43.6 at t-0w) crosses the threshold at which discretionary trip-making restarts, because transit use is the leading edge of non-essential movement. Once crossed, retail trips follow transit within two weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC above its trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by >= 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -50.4 at t-1w to -43.6 at t-0w, a +6.8 point weekly gain
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT gains at least 5 points week-on-week, RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is equal to or lower than its preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Retail recovery requires simultaneous reversal of both mobility margins: transit must rise while time spent at home falls. With TRANSIT at -43.6 and RESIDENTIAL down to 9.4 from 14.9 four weeks earlier, the two series are now moving in the complementary direction, which unlocks discretionary retail trips over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +10 while TRANSIT rises week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 14.9 at t-3w to 9.4 at t-0w while TRANSIT rose from -51.0 to -43.6
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL is below +10 and TRANSIT rises week-on-week, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last-28-day mean in a majority of such weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Late-spring outdoor activity competes directly with indoor retail for discretionary time. PARKS spiked to 43.0 at t-2w before settling at 20.9, showing the population will substitute outdoors whenever weather permits. Any week in which PARKS again exceeds +40 will divert recreation spending away from shops, pushing RETAIL_REC below its trailing mean.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached 43.0 at t-2w then fell to 17.3 at t-1w and 20.9 at t-0w
regime_hint: warm-weather reopening with outdoor-leisure capacity available
failure_condition: Weeks with PARKS above +40 are followed by RETAIL_REC 14-day means that are equal to or higher than the preceding 14-day means.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy movement is the least fear-sensitive series; its recovery to -17.1 at t-0w from -22.6 at t-1w shows households re-normalising habitual in-person errands. As routine errand behaviour normalises, the psychological cost of non-essential store visits falls, so retail-and-recreation traffic rises over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM recovered to -17.1 at t-0w from -22.6 at t-1w
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM improves week-on-week, the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under the Phase-2 reopening regime in Lombardy, restriction easing is the binding constraint on retail capacity, so continued policy relaxation translates almost one-for-one into retail traffic. The joint climb of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT away from their troughs is the signature of that easing, and RETAIL_REC will therefore be higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved to -25.4 and TRANSIT to -43.6 by t-0w, both above their t-3w troughs
failure_condition: While the reopening regime persists and both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay above their t-3w levels, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days falls below its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Discretionary retail requires both routine-necessity trips and commuting trips to be running at once; neither alone is sufficient. The joint recovery of GROCERY_PHARM to -17.1 and TRANSIT to -43.6 in the most recent week satisfies that joint condition, producing a short-latency lift in RETAIL_REC within roughly one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT both improve week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:in the t-1w to t-0w step GROCERY_PHARM rose from -22.6 to -17.1 and TRANSIT from -50.4 to -43.6
failure_condition: Weeks in which both GROCERY_PHARM and TRANSIT improve are followed by a 7-day RETAIL_REC mean that is not above the preceding 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility remains 9.4 points above baseline even after four weeks of reopening, indicating a persistent cohort that continues to work, eat and recreate at home. That stickiness caps the pool of potential shoppers, so as long as RESIDENTIAL stays above +8 the retail recovery stalls and RETAIL_REC stays below its trailing mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL never fell below +9.4 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: While RESIDENTIAL stays above +8, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or above its previous 14-day mean.
